cases.name: Andrea Jean Farrington
cases.narrative: The two had a mostly text-messaging relationship, but Farrington broke that off on 6/12/2015. That day as she was working at the Iowa Children's Museum information desk inside the mall, he shot her three times in the back and fled.

cases.name: Amber Nicole Martin
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Amber was born November 8, 1984, in Louisiana, MO. She grew up in Pike County and attended school in the Bowling Green R-1 School system, where she played Volleyball for the BGHS Lady Cats. Upon graduating in 2003, Amber attended Truman State University where she earned her bachelor’s degree. She was currently in the process of earning her master’s degree in medical laboratory science from the University of Cincinnati.

Growing up, Amber attended Mt. Zion Baptist Church in rural Bowling Green. She enjoyed reading, painting, crafting and riding her bike.

From March of 2013, until August of 2025, Amber worked as a lead medical laboratory scientist at Quincy Medical Group, in Quincy, IL. She recently moved to Coralville, IA in September, where she accepted a position as a medical laboratory scientist supervisor in microbiology at the University of Iowa Health Center."

She worked as a supervisor medical laboratory scientist in the university’s Pathology Department in the past. The couple had relocated from Quincy, Illinois, in August, where they both were employed at Quincy Medical Group, according to reporting by the Muddy River News in Quincy. Amber, who was originally from Bowling Green, Mo., was a microbiology lead medical lab scientist and James was a hematology lead medical technologist. 

Ann Ostermiller, Amber’s former supervisor in Quincy, told a Muddy River News reporter on Monday that she trained Amber for her job, before she retired from the position. “Amber was such a wonderful woman,” Ostermiller said in the interview. “She was vivacious, kind, and loved by all her co-workers.”

Connie Floerchinger, Amber’s supervisor at UIHC, previously told Muddy River News: “She was sweet, smart and had an amazing personality,” Floerchinger said in the interview on Monday. “She had only been with us since September but we all feel like we had known her forever.”
cases.narrative: According to a criminal complaint, Martin, in the hours leading up to the incident at 6:40 a.m., “formulated” a plan to kill his wife in their home. He armed himself with a kitchen knife and surprised her as she came out of another room, repeatedly stabbing her. Amber died at the scene.
